content.comment_body: My [product_name] software only connects to my hardware when I start up with a serial mouse plugged in. After Windows is loaded, I remove the mouse and connect my hardware, otherwise I get a 'device not connected' error. Has anyone encountered this? I've already checked for other programs or devices using the serial port, but nothing helped.
Hi [user_name]! Do you have a second serial port available? Are you using a serial mouse, or a PS2 or USB mouse? I use a USB-to-serial adapter and it works without any issues.
I'm also using a USB-to-serial converter and it works well. The driver creates virtual serial ports so I can select a different port instead of the one used by the mouse, which avoids conflicts.

analysis.insight_summary: A user experiences difficulties connecting software to hardware via the serial port, requiring a workaround involving a serial mouse at startup. Other users indicate that using USB-to-serial adapters resolves such connection problems, suggesting that compatibility or resource conflicts may be causing the issue.
analysis.user_expectations: User hopes for easy and stable hardware connection through the serial port, without complicated steps or workarounds.
